name: Trane Technologies
theme: Data-centre chillers + modular thermal plants + liquid cooling
thesis: Trane is a high-quality, scaled thermal-management platform whose data-centre exposure is becoming more vertically integrated. Core chiller and HVAC capabilities are now complemented by Stellar Energy's modular cooling plants and LiquidStack's direct-to-chip and immersion cooling, giving Trane a credible central-plant-to-chip architecture rather than a single-product AI cooling story.
catalysts: Record commercial HVAC bookings and backlog, conversion of applied-equipment orders, integration and scaling of Stellar Energy and LiquidStack, rising rack densities, broader adoption of liquid cooling, and continued data-centre capacity additions.
risks: Valuation is already premium, with forward P/E around the high-20s/low-30s in August 2026. Q2 adjusted operating margin fell 60 bps year over year despite strong growth, so execution and mix matter. A hyperscaler capex slowdown, cooling overcapacity, acquisition integration issues, or weaker EMEA margins could compress both earnings expectations and the multiple.
valuationTechnical: The business quality and backlog justify a premium, but TT should not be chased purely as an AI theme. Current valuation is materially above slower-growth industrial peers, so the preferred setup is either earnings revisions that outpace multiple expansion or pullbacks where the data-centre backlog remains intact.
researchNote: Q2 2026 organic bookings rose 37%, Americas Commercial HVAC bookings rose 50%, applied-equipment bookings rose 130%, and record backlog reached $12.1bn, up 70%. Book-to-bill was 123%. Revenue grew 11% reported and 9% organically; adjusted EPS rose 11%, while adjusted operating margin declined 60 bps. Trane completed the LiquidStack acquisition in March 2026 and Stellar Energy acquisition in February 2026, expanding from chillers and heat rejection into modular cooling plants, liquid distribution, direct-to-chip and immersion cooling. This breadth is the key reason TT clears the Power Stack promotion bar at 8.4 rather than remaining only a theme watch candidate.
whatMarketsWillWatch: Backlog conversion and whether applied-equipment order growth turns into sustained revenue growth
Data-centre contribution from Stellar Energy and LiquidStack becoming material rather than narrative
Margin recovery after Q2 adjusted operating margin declined 60 bps
Whether book-to-bill remains above 1x as hyperscaler capex normalises
Integration execution and cross-selling from central plant to chip-level cooling
EMEA margin recovery and whether weakness remains contained
